reports.title: Uber Announces Results for Third Quarter 2026

guidance.heading: Outlook for Q4 2026
section: •Gross Bookings of $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion, representing growth of 18% to 22% YoY on a constant-currency basis.
◦Our outlook assumes a roughly 1 percentage-point currency headwind to total reported YoY growth.
•Non-GAAP EPS of $0.95 to $0.99, representing growth of 34% to 39% YoY.
◦Our outlook translates to Adjusted EBITDA of $3.13 billion to $3.23 billion.

desk.headline: Gross bookings up 20% to $59.8bn, non-GAAP EPS up 35% to $0.88; Q4 bookings outlook in line with estimates
results: Trips rose 16% to 4.1bn and gross bookings 20% to $59.8bn; revenue grew a slower 10% to $14.8bn because of business-model changes (an 8-point drag).
Delivery led: bookings up 22% and revenue up 23%; Mobility bookings rose 18% but Mobility revenue slipped 2%.
Non-GAAP operating income rose 38% to $2.3bn, a record 3.9% of bookings; non-GAAP EPS rose 35% to $0.88.
GAAP EPS fell to $0.25 from $3.11: this year includes a $476m loss on equity stakes, last year a $4.9bn tax benefit.
Free cash flow was $2.5bn; $750m of shares were bought back and unrestricted cash stood at $10.1bn.

guidance.summary: For Q4 Uber expects gross bookings of $63.25–65.25bn (18–22% growth in constant currency) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.95–0.99, up 34–39%. One report put the bookings consensus at $64.3bn, around the midpoint.

points: International Mobility was below plan because driver numbers lagged strong rider demand; higher fuel costs from the Middle East conflict hurt markets such as Brazil and India.
Uber is shifting incentive spending from riders to drivers, and says driver hours growth picked up in October.
Delivery growth was credited to more restaurants, grocery and retail (a $15bn annual run rate, up 40%) and Uber One membership of about 55m.
Self-driving: about 700 driverless cars on Uber by year-end, over 2,000 in 2027, with outside financing expected to fund larger fleets.
Management said it will slow acquisitions and focus on integrating recent deals; 2027 priorities are organic growth, autonomy and buybacks.
call.source: Call transcript: The Motley Fool, 4 Nov 2026; consensus: BigGo Finance, 4 Nov 2026
